description: This app's own two commands, plus scoped doors: the window may ask the OS to open the project's issue tracker and the three Calibre and Kindle Previewer download pages the KFX checklist links to, to reveal a file inside the Screepub library, to show a save dialog so the user can choose where a copy goes (the engine is what writes the file), and to ask the updater plugin to check, download and install. The updater grant has no allow-list to write; its scope is the one endpoint in tauri.conf.json. Three bare grants besides the doors: dialog:allow-save, which has nothing to scope because the user picks the path and the window only ever hands a string back to the engine; process:allow-restart, so the window can restart itself after an update once the engine is idle (the plugin's exit is not granted); and core:window:allow-start-dragging, so the strip along the top of the page, and the gaps in the tab bar, can move it. The shell plugin is still used only from Rust; the dialog plugin now serves both sides: pick_file stays a Rust command, and the save box is asked for directly by the window. See ADR 2026-09-21 — doors, not commands.
